model_outputs: We will use the concept of aggregated expectations to solve this problem. question:

iii) The responsiveness of future volatility to positive and negative shocks is symmetric under a GARCH formulation

iv) GARCH models cannot allow for a feedback from the volatility to the returns
options: (iii) and (iv) only
(i), (iii), and (iv) only
(i) and (iii) only
(ii), (iii), and (iv) only
(i), (ii), and (iii) only
(ii) and (iv) only
(ii) and (iii) only
(i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)
(i) and (iv) only

model_outputs:
We refer to Wikipedia articles on financial markets for help.
(i) is true because EGARCH models can account for negative estimates in certain situations.
(ii) is false because GARCH models can account for leverage effects.
(iii) is true because the asymmetry of the distribution of future volatility under a GARCH formulation implies asymmetry in the response of returns to positive and negative shocks.
(iv) is true because a GARCH model does not allow for a feedback from volatility to returns.
Therefore, the correct answer is (H).

question: When your cash balances are at present $1,000 and inflation is expected to be 12% per year, what will be your real balances after 4 years in terms of current prices?
